name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in dry-run mode on a single low-traffic branch in the main repo. This lets us test the tool’s impact without risking disruption, while giving us real data on its behavior. The trade-off is delayed feedback—we won’t catch issues in merged PRs immediately—but the risk of breaking main is too high to justify a live run first. Once we validate the dry-run results, we can expand to merged PRs with known issues to refine the approach.

name: Gauge
text: Dry-run misses the real failure mode: PR-Agent’s misses stay invisible until a real PR fails, and the tool’s blind spots (like cerebras model id 404) won’t surface until we hit a live merge. Instead, run it on a *staging branch* with known bad code—force it to flag issues we can verify, or it’s just noise. Settle it by comparing its output to a manual review on the same branch; if it misses the same things we do, the tool’s useless.

name: Overhaul
text: Run PR-Agent on a *merged* PR with known issues to measure real catch-rate without risking new failures. This costs one PR’s worth of noise but gives hard data on whether the tool actually improves quality.
